npcs.name: Divya Nair
npcs.bio: 25, designs bus shelters nobody notices and libraries everybody does. Opinionated about chairs.

npcs.name: Rohan Iyer
npcs.bio: 26, junior resident at the government hospital. Sleeps four hours, laughs easily, cooks one dish extremely well.

npcs.name: Zoya Sheikh
npcs.role: Product designer you matched with online
npcs.bio: 26, designs banking apps by day and draws comics by night. Will judge your phone's font size.

npcs.name: Kabir Malhotra
npcs.bio: 27, covers city politics, reads three newspapers a day and still thinks print will make a comeback.

start.speaker: amma
start.text: Amma puts a plastic folder on the table with ceremony. 'Just look,' she says. 'Looking is free.' Inside: two biodatas with photos taken in very good lighting.

choices.label: 'I'm not sure I want to get married at all.'

divya.speaker: divya
divya.text: Coffee at a quiet café, both families pretending not to hover. Divya asks what you'd change about your city. You talk for two hours about footpaths. It's the best first meeting you could have hoped for.

rohan.speaker: rohan
rohan.text: Rohan arrives late from a hospital shift, apologises three times, then makes you laugh so hard you spill your tea. 'I'm better when I've slept,' he says. You'd like to find out.

onEnter.text: He came straight from a night shift and still made you laugh.

self.speaker: narrator
self.text: Amma sighs the sigh of every mother in history. 'Fine. But not too late.' The folder goes back in the cupboard, not the bin.

none.speaker: narrator
none.text: Amma doesn't speak to you for the rest of the evening. The next morning there's coffee made the way you like it. That's how she says 'I'm trying'.

events.title: The Families Want an Answer
events.summary: After weeks of meetings, both families are waiting.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Weeks of phone calls, two dinners and one disastrous family lunch later, the question arrives: 'So? Shall we fix a date?'

choices.label: Ask for more time to get to know each other.
It doesn't feel right. Say no, kindly.

yes.speaker: narrator
yes.text: They hesitate. 'I like you,' they say, 'but I don't know you yet. Can we keep meeting before anyone fixes anything?' The families grumble. You're both relieved.

engaged.speaker: narrator
engaged.text: Two families, one living room, too many sweets. A small ring ceremony, and a wedding date the astrologer and the calendar finally agree on.

onEnter.text: The day you both said yes.

time.speaker: narrator
time.text: They agree, gratefully. Getting to know someone properly turns out to be a series of small evenings.

no.speaker: narrator
no.text: It's an awkward phone call and a kind one. The families exchange polite messages and move on. Amma doesn't say 'I told you so', loudly.

events.title: Swipe Right?
events.summary: A dating app, two promising profiles.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Kavya installs a dating app on your phone 'for research' and hands it back. Two profiles stand out.

choices.label: Swipe right on Zoya — product designer, 26, 'will draw you as a cartoon'.
Swipe right on Kabir — journalist, 27, 'ask me about local politics (or don't)'.
Delete the app. Not your thing.

zoya.speaker: zoya
zoya.text: It's a match. Zoya messages first: a cartoon of you, unflattering and accurate. Your first date is a comic-book store and a plate of biryani. You're seeing each other now.

onEnter.text: A comic-book store and a plate of biryani.

kabir.speaker: kabir
kabir.text: It's a match. Kabir's first message is a three-paragraph opinion about your city's bus routes. Your first date lasts until the café closes. You're seeing each other now.

onEnter.text: You talked until the café closed.

nomatch.speaker: narrator
nomatch.text: No match. The app suggests forty-seven other people you might like. You close it and go for a walk instead.

delete.speaker: narrator
delete.text: Deleted. Kavya calls you a dinosaur. You call it peace.

events.title: The Question
events.summary: You've been together a long time. Is this forever?

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: An ordinary evening, and the thought arrives fully formed: you want to marry this person.

variants.text: Arjun is tuning his guitar and humming the song he wrote about samosas.
Nila is photographing the light on your hands, again.

choices.label: Propose with your grandmother's old ring.
Admit it isn't working, and end it kindly.

yes.speaker: narrator
yes.text: You barely get the words out. They say yes before you finish, then make you ask properly so they can say yes again.

onEnter.text: You proposed. They said yes — twice.

wait.speaker: narrator
wait.text: They hold your hands and say, gently, 'Not while we're fighting this much. Ask me again when we're better.' It hurts, and it's fair.

later.speaker: narrator
later.text: You keep the thought to yourself, for now. It'll still be true later.

end.speaker: narrator
end.text: It's the hardest conversation of your life so far. You both cry, then share the last cup of chai. Some endings are done well.

events.title: The Wedding
events.summary: Two families, one budget, a hundred opinions.

start.speaker: amma
start.text: The wedding is three weeks away and the budget meeting has become a negotiation between two families, one caterer and an astrologer.

variants.text: Your father has already spoken to a five-star hotel 'just to ask'.
The whole village expects to be invited. The whole village.

choices.label: A registry wedding, just close family (₹2,000).
Court wedding and a dinner for fifty (₹25,000).
Mid-size wedding, part-funded by a ₹1,00,000 personal loan.
choices.hint: A loan for a party: a familiar Indian story.

choices.label: The big fat wedding — 800 guests, three days (₹15,00,000).

married.speaker: narrator
married.text: Garlands, rice, a hundred photographs and one aunty crying the entire time. You're married.

variants.text: Eight hundred guests, three caterers, one horse that refused to cooperate. People will talk about it for years.
Small, quiet and entirely yours. You remember every face in the room.

choices.label: Honeymoon in Goa for a week (₹45,000).

honeymoon.speaker: narrator
honeymoon.text: Sea or hills, the best part is the same: nobody asking when you'll have children. (They ask the day you get back.)

skip.speaker: narrator
skip.text: You spend the money on a sofa. It's a very good sofa.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: A year into marriage, every relative has asked the question. Tonight, your partner does too — gently. 'What do we want?'

choices.label: Not yet — in a couple of years.

effects.note: Time to talk about children again

try.speaker: narrator
try.text: You both agree. Terrified and excited, in roughly equal measure.

adopt.speaker: narrator
adopt.text: You start the paperwork with an agency. It will take months. You're both sure.

later.speaker: narrator
later.text: You agree to wait. The relatives do not agree. That's their problem.

none.speaker: narrator
none.text: You're on the same page, which is what matters. Amma takes a while to accept it.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: 3:40 a.m., a hospital corridor, a nurse who has done this a thousand times saying 'Congratulations'. Small, loud and perfect.

choices.label: Let your partner pick the name.

born.speaker: narrator
born.text: Amma holds the baby and cries. Then she starts giving advice and doesn't stop for eighteen years.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The agency calls on a Tuesday afternoon. A toddler with enormous eyes and a stuffed elephant. 'Whenever you're ready,' the social worker says. You've been ready for months.

choices.label: Let your partner pick the name.

born.speaker: narrator
born.text: The elephant gets its own pillow. Amma knits it a sweater.

onEnter.text: The day the grandchild came home.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Your child asks for a sibling — specifically 'a baby brother or a puppy'. Your partner looks at you.

no.speaker: narrator
no.text: You compromise on a goldfish. It is named after a cricketer.

events.title: Cracks
events.summary: An argument that isn't really about the dishes.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: It starts with the dishes and ends somewhere much older: money, time, who gives up more. You both go to bed angry.

counsel.speaker: narrator
counsel.text: The counsellor makes you each say what you need without saying 'you always'. It's harder than any exam you've sat.

trip.speaker: narrator
trip.text: Two days away from everything. You remember you actually like each other.

good.speaker: narrator
good.text: It's a long night. By the end of it you understand each other better than you have in months.

bad.speaker: narrator
bad.text: The conversation goes in circles and ends in silence. Tomorrow you'll try again.

ignore.speaker: narrator
ignore.text: It blows over. Things that blow over tend to blow back.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Neither of you remembers the last good day. The silence in the flat has a weight to it.

variants.text: The children have started asking why everyone is so quiet.

saved.speaker: narrator
saved.text: It's not a fairytale fix. It's slow, deliberate work. But you're both still at the table.

amicable.speaker: narrator
amicable.text: Lawyers, paperwork, the division of a life into two piles. You manage to stay kind. That will matter for years.

variants.text: You agree on shared custody and a rule: never fight in front of the kids.

fight.speaker: narrator
fight.text: Months of hearings and bills. When it's over, nobody feels like they won.

events.title: Gone in a Second
events.summary: Your phone disappears on a crowded bus.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: A crowded bus, a sudden lurch, and your pocket is lighter. Your phone is gone — photos, contacts, everything.

choices.label: File a police complaint and block the IMEI.
Buy a Kiwi Note to get by (₹11,999).
Live without a smartphone for a while.

fir.speaker: narrator
fir.text: The constable writes everything down slowly and says 'we will inform you'. They never do. At least nobody can use it now.

recovered.speaker: narrator
recovered.text: Three weeks later, the police call: they caught a gang with forty phones. Yours is one of them, screen cracked but alive.

bought.speaker: narrator
bought.text: A cheap phone and a long evening restoring your contacts. Lesson learned: front pocket on buses.

live.speaker: narrator
live.text: No phone. It's inconvenient for a week, then strangely peaceful.

events.title: Fender Bender
events.summary: A scooter cuts across, you swerve into a divider.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: A scooter cuts across without looking. You swerve, and the divider wins. Nobody's hurt; your bumper is in two pieces.

choices.label: Claim insurance (₹5,000 deductible, 10 days without the car).
Pay the garage in cash and keep your no-claim bonus (₹38,000).

claim.speaker: narrator
claim.text: Forms, photographs, a surveyor who sighs a lot. Ten days later the car comes back looking almost new.

cash.speaker: narrator
cash.text: Expensive, but next year's insurance premium will thank you.

events.title: Traffic Challan
events.summary: A traffic cop flags you down.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: A traffic constable waves you over. Signal jump, apparently. The camera agrees. ₹1,000.

choices.label: Contest it in traffic court (a lost day).

pay.speaker: narrator
pay.text: Paid. You notice the signal timings a lot more after that.

court.speaker: narrator
court.text: A morning in a queue, two minutes before a magistrate. Fine upheld, plus court fees.

waived.speaker: narrator
waived.text: The camera timestamp is wrong by three seconds. Case dismissed. You feel like a lawyer.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Chest pain at 2 a.m. An ambulance, an ECG, a cardiologist who looks at your reports and then at you. 'This is a warning,' she says. 'Next time it may not be.'

variants.text: 'And the cigarettes,' she adds. 'All of them. Today.'

choices.label: Change everything — quit habits, exercise, sleep.
Take the medicines, try to cut down.

overhaul.speaker: narrator
overhaul.text: It's not one decision; it's a thousand small ones. But you make the first one in the hospital bed, and you keep making them.

meds.speaker: narrator
meds.text: The pills help. The habits stay. The doctor asks you to come back in three months.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: HR's email has one line and an attachment: a festival bonus of ₹25,000. The office is suddenly very cheerful.

choices.label: Send half home and treat the family.

save.speaker: narrator
save.text: Straight into savings. Future you nods approvingly.

family.speaker: narrator
family.text: Amma calls to say you shouldn't have, then tells all the neighbours that you did.

splurge.speaker: narrator
splurge.text: New clothes, a nice dinner, and a little guilt that tastes fine.

events.title: A Regular in the Chair
events.summary: The salon owner has noticed you.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Meena, who owns the salon, finishes your trim and says, 'You always watch how I hold the scissors. Want to learn properly? Assistant job, evenings and weekends.'

yes.speaker: narrator
yes.text: Your first lesson: sweeping. Your second lesson: sweeping better. By the third week, she lets you hold the scissors.

no.speaker: narrator
no.text: 'Offer stands,' Meena says. 'Ask anytime.' (The assistant job is listed at the salon.)

epilogueLines.text: You're married. Some days it's easy and some days it's work, and you both keep showing up.
There are small shoes by the door now. Your life is louder, more tired, and fuller than you imagined.
Your marriage ended, but kindly. You still wish each other well on birthdays.
The divorce was bitter and expensive. Healing is slower than the paperwork was.
